LESSON: LEVERS AS SIMPLE MACHINES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 3.2: Levers as simple machines

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Levers as simple machines. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are levers used in day to day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify common levers used in day- to-day life
2. describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier
3. classify levers into the three classes
4. demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier
5. appreciate the use of levers in making work easier

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LEVERS AS SIMPLE MACHINES
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Levers as simple machines helps you succeed in SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: LEVERS AS SIMPLE MACHINES
Study Levers as simple machines like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify common levers used in day- to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to identify common levers used in day- to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify common levers used in day- to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Levers as simple machines” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify common levers used in day- to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier

What this means
In this part you learn to describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Levers as simple machines matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Classify levers into the three classes

What this means
In this part you learn to classify levers into the three classes. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify levers into the three classes.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Levers as simple machines this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify levers into the three classes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Levers as simple machines” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Appreciate the use of levers in making work easier

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of levers in making work easier. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of levers in making work easier.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Levers as simple machines matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of levers in making work easier. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Levers as simple machines is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Levers as simple machines” around your school. (skill: identify common levers used in day- to-day life)

Example 2: Say why Levers as simple machines matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Levers as simple machines this week. (skill: classify levers into the three classes)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Levers as simple machines” around your school. (skill: demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Levers as simple machines to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify common levers used in day- to-day life.
3. Practise this skill: describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier.
4. Practise this skill: classify levers into the three classes.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Levers as simple machines from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Levers as simple machines: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Levers as simple machines?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are levers used in day to day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Levers as simple machines means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify common levers used in day- to-day life.
5. Be able to: describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
